question.problem:
Consider the following parabola:

$$
x=15{t}^{2},\,y=3t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

The Cartesian equation of the parabola is

${y}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{x}{15},\,t=\frac{y}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{x}{15}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =\frac{x}{15} \\ {y}^{2} & =\frac{3}{5}x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${y}^{2}=\frac{3}{5}x.$
